title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We present the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a preregistered descriptive summary, label any one‑sided McNemar as exploratory (post‑hoc), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but also raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) designed to isolate purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions so that any paired difference is attributable to deterministic validation and the permitted repair call, not to first‑pass generation differences such as prompt engineering or sampling variance.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from a synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces; (2) complete execution accounting and artifact grounding (completed pairs = 1000; hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; repair calls = 5; model_configuration records temperature = null/unset); (3) preregistered confirmatory inference (exact two‑sided McNemar) together with preregistered descriptive summaries (paired bootstrap CI) and clear labeling of any post‑hoc exploratory tests.
sections.related_work:
LLM outputs for structured tasks are known to suffer from hallucinations and prompt sensitivity that materially affect correctness for code and configuration outputs; syntheses and controlled experiments document these modes and motivate verifier‑assisted workflows [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning reduce syntactic and executable errors in several structured domains, though many demonstrations come from domains outside NetOps and depend on tool/validator fidelity for transfer [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system work emphasizes verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and governance/proof‑carrying proposals to mitigate automation risks; these works present prototypes and argue that operational reliability depends heavily on validator coverage and externally enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements this literature by preregistering a paired comparison whose estimand isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single limited repair call when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions. This avoids conflating downstream interventions with first‑pass prompt/decoding differences and clarifies the contribution and limits of validation+repair layers under tightly controlled conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design fidelity. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key predeclared elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 drawn deterministically from challenging_workflow_stress_v1; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per pair reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries included a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failures as unsafe.

Interpretive constraints from shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled candidate; the guarded pipeline may deterministically reject that candidate and invoke at most one permitted repair. Under this design, paired outcome differences can arise only from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). The study therefore does not measure effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, or constrained decoding arms that were not executed.

Model and validator configuration. The declared model/provider (execution/model_configuration.json) is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0), which enforces the task manifest's required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, protected‑field constraints, and emits a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict.

Task corpus, selection rule, and missingness. Tasks were selected deterministically using the preregistered ordinal rule producing exactly 1000 unique tasks. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments. The executor used the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' missingness treatment; sensitivity analyses treating failures as unsafe were preregistered but not needed because failed episodes = 0.

Statistical analysis. The preregistered confirmatory test is the exact two‑sided McNemar test on the 2×2 contingency table of paired outcomes. The paired bootstrap percentile interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was preregistered as a descriptive secondary summary. Multiplicity adjustments for secondary hypotheses were preregistered (Holm–Bonferroni) but no secondary confirmatory hypotheses are claimed here.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑grounded). The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 (cache_miss_count = 1005) and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}; total model calls used = 1005.

Primary paired outcomes. The 2×2 paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Preregistered inferential and descriptive summaries. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; by the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 this does not support H1. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]; this CI is a preregistered descriptive summary only. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125, but because a one‑sided test was NOT prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is explicitly reported as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not alter the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Repair traces and diagnostics. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5). Representative episode artifacts show the validator rejecting an initial candidate for required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches, the adapter invoking the single allowed repair call, and the validator accepting the repaired candidate on revalidation. Contamination checks found no prompt leakage; missingness_summary.csv records zero failed or unscorable episodes. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived as described in the execution manifest.
sections.discussion:
Inferential primacy and the bootstrap: preregistered confirmatory inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625) and therefore the preregistered H1 is not supported at α = 0.05. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) was preregistered as a descriptive summary; with extremely sparse discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0) the bootstrap percentile method can produce a CI that excludes zero while the exact paired test remains non‑significant. This apparent tension is a sampling‑mechanism artifact: near‑unity baseline rates produce very few discordant pairs, yielding discrete exact test p‑values that can exceed α even when resampling‑based summaries indicate small positive effects. We emphasize the inferential hierarchy declared in the preregistration: the exact McNemar result is the confirmatory outcome; bootstrap summaries are descriptive and sensitive to sparse discordant counts and should not be interpreted as overturning the preregistered test.

Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both arms reused the same initial sampled candidate, any paired improvement arises only from deterministic validation and the permitted single repair. The observed five repairs demonstrate that a validator with sufficient coverage can correct some ordering/sequence violations. The small absolute improvement (0.005) and the sparse discordant count circumscribe generality: (a) the synthetic corpus and model+prompt pairing produced an unusually high baseline validity (0.995), (b) validator coverage determines which error classes are detectable/correctable, and (c) expanding the generator variance (independent first‑pass generations) or repair budget could alter effect sizes.

Threats to validity and follow‑ups. Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity is strengthened by preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and deterministic seeding, but this design precludes measuring first‑pass generation interventions. External validity is limited by single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini) and a synthetic corpus. Conclusion validity is limited by sparse discordant counts and a preregistered power plan that assumed a much lower baseline (≈0.60); the observed baseline (0.995) therefore materially reduced power to detect small absolute gains. Recommended preregistered follow‑ups (artifact‑supported): (1) run an unshared (independent generation) arm to measure prompt/decoding interventions; (2) sweep repair budgets to estimate marginal returns; (3) expand validator rule sets and topology heterogeneity; (4) evaluate multiple model families with power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The preregistered exact McNemar is the confirmatory outcome; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) computed post‑hoc is explicitly labeled exploratory. These artifact‑grounded results indicate verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity, repair budget, and whether initial generation variance is permitted. All preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, analysis artifacts, and deterministic reconciliation files are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups.

Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the deterministic validator/digital twin. Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Immutable initial master‑prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. After the autonomy lock, literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and automated revisions were performed by the autonomous research run; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw model outputs, validator traces, analysis artifacts, and deterministic reconciliation files are archived with the run (see execution manifest in the evidence bundle).
limitations: Single‑model scope: only gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) was evaluated; results do not generalize across models or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks are drawn from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect = 0.15, so the observed baseline reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains via the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; any one‑sided McNemar reported was post‑hoc and labeled exploratory.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
